title: C.H. Robinson releases Edge Report: August freight market insights
summary: Read the August Edge Report for insights on tariffs, global supply-chain risks, carrier vetting, and freight market trends.
body_text: C.H. Robinson releases Edge Report: August freight market insights August report examines new tariff framework, ongoing Middle East conflict, and regulatory changes impacting the freight industry Copy to clipboard Copy to clipboard Link Copied 2026-08-12 | News Read by more than 14,000 logistics leaders each month, the C.H. Robinson Edge Report brings together market data, expert analysis, and actionable guidance to help shippers stay ahead of volatility and plan with confidence. This month’s edition examines how tightening capacity, rising transportation costs, and evolving trade and regulatory policies are influencing freight markets around the world. From the new Section 301 tariff framework and Middle East volatility affecting global supply chains to the increased scrutiny of carrier vetting practices, the report highlights key trends shippers should monitor and strategies to help navigate them. What insights are inside the August 2026 Edge Report? Freight market: Get updated insights across truckload , less-than-truckload (LTL), intermodal, ocean shipping, air freight , and ports and drayage. Learn how tightening truckload capacity and rising LTL costs are creating new planning challenges for shippers, and explore strategies to help manage transportation spend. See where softer ocean demand is creating more flexibility and where constraints remain, and how air freight pressure is becoming more localized across specific origins, commodities, and time-sensitive cargo flows. Canada, Mexico, and cross-border: See how stricter B-1 visa enforcement, English-language requirements, and increased scrutiny of freight documentation are tightening cross-border capacity in Mexico. Find out how the cross-border market is evolving, how the Gordie Howe International Bridge could improve the resiliency of U.S.-Canada freight flows, and why new tariffs on Canadian goods may soon have an impact. Trade policy and government regulations: Explore the new Section 301 tariff framework and what continued uncertainty around U.S. trade policy and USMCA negotiations could mean in the months ahead. Understand how the Supreme Court’s broker liability decision and evolving requirements for carrier safety, driver qualifications, and transportation infrastructure are reshaping the freight landscape. Industry insights: Get sector-specific perspectives for retail , automotive, energy , and healthcare supply chains. Learn what the latest Consumer Price Index data means for retail supply chains, how connected-vehicle code restrictions are affecting automotive sourcing, what the nuclear energy comeback could mean for energy logistics, and how the growing rural hospital crisis is creating new challenges for healthcare supply chains. Diesel fuel: Learn how shifting global fuel markets are creating different levels of exposure across Europe, Asia, and North America, and what renewed diesel volatility could mean for freight costs and planning. The August Edge Report Is Now Live As market conditions and trade policies continue to evolve, the August Edge Report provides the clarity logistics leaders need to adapt and stay resilient. Read the full report and download the shareable highlights to inform your planning for the months ahead. title: CSXT HDF Fuel Index Rate Adjustment Update for September 1, 2026
summary: CSX is a leading supplier of rail-based freight transportation in North America. But there's more to CSX than you might expect. Learn all about CSX and discover what we're doing for our customers, environment and communities. Visit http://www.csx.com/.
body_text: CSXT HDF Fuel Index Rate Adjustment Update for September 1, 2026 Released: August 19, 2026 Dear CSX Transportation Customer, Following is the CSX Transportation HDF Fuel Index Rate Adjustment (8661) amount effective September 1, 2026. CSXT HDF/Mileage Based Fuel Index Rate Adjustment (8662) The highway diesel fuel/mileage based fuel surcharge published in CSXT Fuel Surcharge Publication 8662 applies to all regulated common carriage and public exempt line haul freight rates existing or established by CSXT on or after June 5, 2026. The CSXT HDF/mileage based fuel surcharge of 32 cents per mile, which became effective August 1, 2026, will change to 31 cents per mile for shipments having a bill of lading dated on or after September 1, 2026. Following are the 8662 CSXT HDF/mileage based fuel surcharge rates: 44 cents per mile effective June 5, 2026 47 cents per mile effective July 1, 2026 32 cents per mile effective August 1, 2026 31 cents per mile effective September 1, 2026 CSXT HDF/Mileage Based Fuel Index Rate Adjustment (8661) The highway diesel fuel/mileage based fuel index rate adjustment is published in CSXT 8661 and applies to all line haul freight rates and charges set forth in contracts, and other pricing documents that reference CSXT Publication 8661 dated on or after April 23, 2007. The CSXT HDF/mileage based fuel index rate adjustment of 76 cents per mile, which became effective August 1, 2026, will change to 74 cents per mile for shipments having a bill of lading dated on or after September 1, 2026. Following are the 8661 CSXT HDF/mileage based fuel index rate adjustments: 46 cents per mile effective January 1, 2026 41 cents per mile effective February 1, 2026 39 cents per mile effective March 1, 2026 44 cents per mile effective April 1, 2026 74 cents per mile effective May 1, 2026 88 cents per mile effective June 1, 2026 91 cents per mile effective July 1, 2026 76 cents per mile effective August 1, 2026 74 cents per mile effective September 1, 2026 The fuel index rate adjustment (contract rates - 8661) amount is based on the "HDF Average Price" of 495.5 cents per gallon for the calendar month of July 2026. The "HDF Average Price" is on U. S. No. 2 Diesel Retail Sales by All Sellers, as determined and published by the U. S. Department of Energy, Energy Information Administration at www.eia.doe.gov . Please address any questions you may have to your CSXT Sales Manager.

title: Restaurant Benchmarking: Compare Delivery Locations Fairly
summary: Compare restaurant delivery locations using fair peer groups, normalized metrics, reliable samples, and a clear action framework.
body_text: Restaurant Benchmarking: Compare Delivery Locations Fairly Your highest-sales location may not be your best-run location. It may operate longer hours, sit in a denser delivery market, or receive more marketplace demand. A smaller store can produce more orders per open hour, cancel fewer orders, and earn stronger ratings - then still land near the bottom of a raw sales ranking. That is the problem restaurant benchmarking should solve. Done well, it separates scale from execution. Done poorly, it turns a spreadsheet into a blame list. Here is how to compare delivery performance fairly and turn real outliers into action. What is restaurant benchmarking? Restaurant benchmarking is the practice of comparing performance against a consistent reference point: another location, a peer group, an earlier period, or an industry range. For delivery operations, fair benchmarking uses comparable stores and normalized rates - such as orders per open hour or cancellations per 100 orders - so teams act on operating differences, not scale alone. There are four useful reference points: Internal benchmark: Compare similar locations in the same brand. Historical benchmark: Compare a store with its own prior performance. Channel benchmark: Compare the same location across delivery platforms. External benchmark: Compare with a credible industry or segment range. Start with internal data, where definitions and operating context are easier to verify. Why do raw location rankings mislead operators? Raw sales tells you which store sold the most. It does not tell you which team executed best. Six factors commonly distort the ranking: Market demand: A dense urban area can generate more demand than a smaller suburb. Open hours: A longer schedule creates more chances to take orders. Store maturity: A new location should not share a baseline with a mature unit. Channel mix: One store may benefit from a marketplace campaign. Promotions: An offer can lift orders while changing order value and customer mix. Sample size: One cancellation in 20 orders creates a volatile 5% rate; ten in 1,000 creates a steadier 1%. The 2025 Off-Premises Restaurant Trends report found that 37% of U.S. adults order delivery weekly. Location comparisons now need the same discipline operators apply to dine-in performance. How do you benchmark delivery locations fairly? Use this eight-step process: Define the decision. State what the comparison should help you decide. Build a peer group. Match stores by concept, market, maturity, volume band, and channel mix. Align the time window. Use the same dates, weekdays, dayparts, and open-hour rules. Check data quality. Flag missing channels, closures, tiny samples, and incomplete hours. Normalize the metrics. Use rates per order or per open hour where scale would distort the result. Use medians and quartiles. Show the middle and the spread, not only the average. Add operating context. Annotate promotions, local events, weather, staffing gaps, and outages. Assign an action and review date. Name the owner, test, expected signal, and next check. Start with the decision because the same metric can support different conversations. A regional manager deciding where to coach needs a different view from a marketing lead deciding where to run an offer. Which delivery metrics belong in the benchmark? A useful scorecard balances volume, reliability, customer experience, and commercial performance. Which productivity metrics show demand relative to opportunity? Orders per open hour: delivered orders divided by marketplace open hours. Sales per open hour: delivery sales divided by marketplace open hours. Average order value: delivery sales divided by completed orders. These metrics reduce the advantage of longer schedules, but different daypart models may still need separate groups. Which reliability metrics show preventable friction? Cancellation rate: canceled orders divided by accepted orders. Store uptime rate: time available to receive orders divided by scheduled marketplace hours. Order-issue rate: confirmed delivery order issues divided by completed orders, when consistently available. Prep or wait-time signal: use the same platform definition across every store. If a definition changes by source, compare within that source or document the difference. Which customer signals show repeated experience gaps? Average rating by location and platform. Share of one- and two-star reviews. Complaint themes such as missing items, cold food, long waits, or packaging failures. Review volume, because a 4.2 rating from 12 reviews is not as stable as a 4.2 from 1,200. Use a restaurant dashboard for delivery operators to keep the scorecard balanced. A store with strong sales and high cancellations is not simply a top performer; it is a high-volume operation with a reliability problem. How do you normalize restaurant metrics? Normalization means expressing results on a common basis. Use per-open-hour metrics for different schedules and per-order rates for different volumes. Keep the numerator and denominator within the same date range, store, platform, and order population. For example: Orders per open hour = completed delivery orders ÷ marketplace open hours Cancellations per 100 accepted orders = canceled orders ÷ accepted orders × 100 Low-rating share = one- and two-star reviews ÷ total reviews × 100 Total sales still matters for resource allocation. Show scale and execution side by side. Consistent definitions are the foundation of useful delivery sales analytics . Keep a one-page metric dictionary that states the source, formula, exclusions, refresh cadence, and owner for every benchmark. Why should you use medians and quartiles? The median - the middle value when stores are sorted - is less affected by one extreme result than the average. Quartiles divide the group into four parts. They help teams see the performance spread: Top quartile: the strongest 25% for the metric. Middle 50%: the normal operating range. Bottom quartile: the 25% that deserve investigation. Bottom quartile should mean “inspect,” not “punish.” Add a minimum sample rule and mark low-volume locations “insufficient sample” until they clear an agreed threshold. The Operator’s Guide to Restaurant Benchmarking makes an important distinction: a benchmark shows the reference point; a KPI measures progress toward a goal. Use both. A store can sit below the peer median today and still be on track if its trend is improving. How should multi-unit brands build peer groups? Start with these filters: Same brand or operating concept. Similar service model and menu complexity. Comparable market type: urban, suburban, small town, campus, or travel hub. Similar store maturity. Similar delivery order-volume band. Similar operating-day and daypart mix. Similar marketplace mix. Do not make the group so narrow that every store becomes unique. Choose the two or three factors most likely to affect the metric, and write the rule before viewing results. How can an independent restaurant benchmark fairly? Use your own restaurant as the peer: Compare the last four complete weeks with the prior four. Compare Mondays with Mondays, not Mondays with Saturdays. Compare lunch, dinner, and late night separately. Compare each delivery platform using the same period. Use a rolling median to reduce the effect of one unusual day. Annotate closures, promotions, weather, holidays, and local events. Set the baseline, make one operating change, and watch the metric that should respond. What does a fair comparison look like? Consider this illustrative four-week example: Store A leads in total sales. Store C leads in sales per open hour. Store B has the lowest cancellation rate. There is no single winner. If the decision is where to add operating hours, Store C deserves a closer demand and capacity review. If the decision is where to investigate cancellations, Store C is also the concern. If the decision is which team may have a reliable acceptance and fulfillment routine worth studying, Store B is the better starting point. That is what good benchmarking does: it turns “Which store is best?” into a more useful question. How do you turn an outlier into action? Ask: Did the metric change suddenly or gradually? Is the gap present on every delivery platform? Is it concentrated by daypart, weekday, or menu category? Did scheduled marketplace hours match actual availability? Was a promotion, outage, closure, or staffing issue active? Is the denominator large enough to trust? What does the stronger peer do differently? Then choose one test. If a peer group has a prep-time gap, review delivery app prep time optimization , change the relevant operating input where appropriate, and remeasure the cohort. Check context before copying a top store’s practice. What should a weekly benchmark review include? Keep the meeting to 30 minutes: Five minutes: Confirm data coverage, closures, and unusual events. Ten minutes: Review the top and bottom quartile by two or three priority metrics. Ten minutes: Choose no more than three outliers for investigation. Five minutes: Assign an owner, action, expected signal, and review date. Maintain a simple decision log: If a benchmark creates no action, narrow the report or the meeting. How can Voosh support location benchmarking? Fair benchmarking is difficult when each delivery platform has its own portal, definitions, filters, and export. Voosh helps restaurant teams centralize third-party-delivery performance data and view relevant signals by store and channel. That makes it easier to compare consistent periods, spot outliers, and move from a brand-level number to the location or platform that needs investigation. Voosh does not replace the operating context only a local team can provide. It also should not be presented as a source of external peer benchmarks unless that capability is specifically confirmed for the customer. Its value here is giving the team a clearer internal comparison layer and reducing the work required to assemble it. Which benchmarking mistakes should teams avoid? Ranking stores by raw sales alone. Comparing different date windows or incomplete weeks. Mixing scheduled hours with actual marketplace availability. Comparing new stores with mature stores without a ramp period. Treating different platform definitions as identical. Using percentages without showing the sample size. Moving the cohort rules after seeing the result. Reporting an outlier without an owner or review date. The 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry highlights persistent cost pressure, uneven traffic, and increased operator interest in digital ordering, automation, and data analytics. That environment makes disciplined comparisons more useful than another leaderboard. Compare fairly, then investigate locally Start with a real question. Compare like with like. Put totals beside normalized rates, show sample size, add local context, assign one action, and measure again. If your delivery data is split across platforms and locations, Voosh can help your team see the internal comparison more clearly. Book a demo to see how Voosh can support store- and channel-level delivery analysis.

title: Soligenix Announces Recent Updates and Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Soligenix, Inc. (Nasdaq: SNGX) (Soligenix or the Company), a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing products to treat rare diseases where there is an unmet medical...
body_text: News Releases Soligenix Announces Recent Updates and Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results PRINCETON, N.J. , Aug. 7, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Soligenix, Inc. (Nasdaq: SNGX) (Soligenix or the Company), a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing products to treat rare diseases where there is an unmet medical need, announced today its recent updates and financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. "While we were disappointed with the outcome of the Phase 3 FLASH2 clincial study that led to discontinuing the HyBryte™ (synthetic hypericin) development program, this outcome does not diminish the strength of our broader pipeline or the strategic value of Soligenix," stated Christopher J. Schaber, PhD, President and Chief Executive Officer of Soligenix. "We remain focused on evaluating opportunities across our diversified portfolio, including the continued advancement of SGX945 (dusquetide) for Behçet's disease, which demonstrated promising preliminary efficacy and was generally safe and well-tolerated in our Phase 2 study, as well as our ThermoVax® heat-stable vaccine platform." "With approximately $9.8 million in cash as of June 30, 2026, providing cash runway into the second quarter of 2028, we are well positioned to actively evaluate all strategic options to maximize stockholder value, including but not limited to partnerships, licensing opportunities, merger and acquisition opportunities, government grants and contracts, and the advancement of our existing pipeline. Maintaining our Nasdaq listing is also an important strategic asset that supports these efforts by preserving access to the public capital markets, enhancing our attractiveness to potential strategic partners and acquirers, and providing additional flexibility as we evaluate these opportunities. Consistent with this strategy, we are contuning to seek non-dilutive funding support for the development of our heat-stable Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine program from various sources, including the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) and others." Soligenix Recent Updates On June 8, 2026, the Company announced that along with the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, it would be applying for CEPI funding to develop a protein-based, thermostable vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo virus by leveraging the thermostability, immunogenicity, and efficacy data demonstrated with its filovirus vaccines. To view this press release, please click here . On May 26, 2026, in response to a recent Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Congo, the Company highlighted previous work with the University of Hawaiʻi, which has demonstrated platform compatibility with the key Bundibugyo virus antigen enabling rapid development of a protein-based thermostable subunit vaccine. To view this press release, please click here . Financial Results – Quarter Ended June 30, 2026 Soligenix had no revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Soligenix's net loss was $2.0 million, or ($0.12) per share, for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $2.7 million, or ($0.82) per share, for the same prior year period. This decrease in net loss was primarily due to a decrease in in research and development expenses associated with the terminated FLASH2 trial and related HyBryte™ development activities. Research and development expenses were $1.0 million as compared to $1.7 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease was primarily due to decreases in costs associated with the terminated FLASH2 trial and related HyBryte™ development activities. General and administrative expenses were $1.1 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 as compared to $1.1 million for the same period in 2025, relatively flat with a de minimis increase. As of June 30, 2026, the Company's cash position was approximately $9.8 million. About Soligenix, Inc. Soligenix is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing products to treat rare diseases where there is an unmet medical need. Our Specialized BioTherapeutics business segment is developing synthetic hypericin for the treatment of psoriasis (SGX302), and our first-in-class Innate Defense Regulator (IDR) technology, dusquetide, for the treatment of inflammatory diseases, including aphthous ulcers in Behçet's Disease (BD) (SGX945) and oral mucositis in head and neck cancer (SGX942). We were developing HyBryte™ (SGX301 or synthetic hypericin sodium), a photodynamic therapy utilizing visible light, for the treatment of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) in a Phase 3 study called "FLASH2" (Fluorescent Light Activated Synthetic Hypericin 2). The Data Monitoring Committee completed its interim efficacy analysis of the FLASH2 trial during April 2026, and under the terms of the interim analysis, the study was recommended to halt for futility. In June 2026, following a thorough review of the Data Monitoring Committee's recommendation and evaluation of the program's path forward, our Board of Directors determined that it was in our best interest and the interest of our stockholders to terminate the HyBryte™ development program. Our Public Health Solutions business segment includes development programs for RiVax®, our ricin toxin vaccine candidate, as well as our vaccine programs targeting filoviruses (such as Marburg and Ebola) and CiVax™, our vaccine candidate for the prevention of COVID-19 (caused by SARS-CoV-2). The development of our vaccine programs incorporates the use of our proprietary heat stabilization platform technology, known as ThermoVax®. To date, this business segment has been supported with government grant and contract funding from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), the Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) and the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA). For further information regarding Soligenix, Inc., please visit the Company's website at https://www.soligenix.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X at @Soligenix_Inc . Statements that are not historical facts, such as "anticipates," "estimates," "believes," "hopes," "intends," "plans," "expects," "goal," "may," "suggest," "will," "potential," or similar expressions, are forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to a number of risks, uncertainties and other factors that could cause actual events or results in future periods to differ materially from what is expressed in, or implied by, these statements, and include the expected timing and results of clinical trials and the expected timing of regulatory submissions and approvals. The Company's submission of an application for funding from CEPI for Bundibugyo virus vaccine development is preliminary in nature and there can be no assurance that CEPI will select the Company's application for funding, that the Company will receive any funding from CEPI, or that any such funding, if received, will be sufficient to advance the Company's vaccine development programs. The Company does not intend to provide updates regarding the status of its CEPI application unless and until a material development occurs, such as the receipt of a funding award. In addition, there can be no assurance as to the timing or success of any of its clinical/preclinical trials. Notwithstanding the result of HyBryte™ (SGX301) in the first Phase 3 clinical trial (or any other studies) for the treatment of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and the Phase 2a clinical trial of SGX302 for the treatment of psoriasis, there can be no assurance as to the timing or success of the clinical trials of SGX302 for the treatment of psoriasis. Additionally, despite the biologic activity observed in aphthous ulcers induced by chemotherapy and radiation, there can be no assurance as to the timing or success of the clinical trials of SGX945 for the treatment of Behçet's Disease. title: Inbound vs outbound sales: Differences, strategies, and when to use each
summary: Compare inbound and outbound sales strategies. Discover how sales teams build pipeline, improve conversion rates, and scale outreach.
body_text: Choosing between inbound and outbound is like choosing between peanut butter and jelly. It's rarely an either/or situation between attraction marketing and cold outreach. Instead, it's a question of ratio and how to make the two work well together. The ideal balance between inbound and outbound depends on your pipeline needs, available resources, and market situation. Inbound and outbound sales solve different pipeline problems Inbound and outbound sales work well together because they target different types of buyers. Inbound uses marketing assets to attract leads who are already researching their problem. Outbound, on the other hand, targets accounts that aren't there yet but would benefit from your help. Together, these two methods help you capture your TAM and maximize lead generation . Inbound sales brings in people already looking Inbound sales is more passive than outbound sales. It's like setting up fishing nets that attract and convert potential customers on autopilot. For example, at Artisan, we use our blog to attract sales leaders to our website, answer their questions, and point them toward our AI BDR software. Inbound sales takes three common forms: SEO: Creating web content that ranks in search engine results pages for queries your target customers ask. Content marketing: Running webinars and publishing blog posts, newsletters, and other types of content that educate your target audience and regularly plug your products or services. Referral systems: Incentivizing existing customers to recommend your business to other potential prospects. These inbound methods showcase your business and encourage leads to move through the sales funnel on their own, resulting in warm leads for your salespeople to close. To illustrate, let's say a business owner types "how do I automate cold email?" into Google. They click a blog post in the search results, read it, and think, "Oh man, this is so helpful!" At the bottom of the blog post, they see an option to attend a web demo about outreach automation and sign up. They submit the form, and just like that, the business has generated a lead. Now, it's time for an inbound sales rep to step in and nurture the lead toward a purchase. Outbound sales goes directly to the right accounts Unlike inbound sales, which depends on leads taking action, outbound is proactive. The outbound sales rep is a hunter: they've defined their ideal customer, and now they're heading out to engage them with personalized cold emails, pitches, and social media touches. Outbound sales takes several common forms: Cold calls: Calling decision-makers, pitching your product or service, and sparking enough interest to book a sales meeting or demo. Cold email: Emailing potential buyers through personalized sequences that touch on likely pain points and relevant needs. Social selling: Interacting with decision-makers on social media and messaging them directly to secure a meeting. The benefit of outbound is that you can target and engage high-value accounts without waiting for them to find your social media ad or blog post. You can research the business, identify likely pain points, engage decision-makers, and spark interest in your solution through tailored messaging and rapport-building. In most cases, the goal of all this cold outreach is a booked meeting, where an account executive will hold a discovery call, learn about the business's needs, and nurture the lead to a close. The main difference is who initiates the interaction Outbound sales includes a step that inbound does not: prospecting. This is when a sales rep actively identifies leads with a view to initiating a conversation. The rep, often a sales development representative (SDR), sends cold emails, makes cold calls, and attempts to spark the lead's interest in your offer. With inbound sales, the opposite happens. The lead initiates the sales opportunity, typically by completing a form or reaching out over phone or email after seeing an ad, blog post, or some other piece of marketing content. The inbound sales rep, therefore, only speaks with interested leads who are already familiar with the brand and its offerings. The differences that actually affect pipeline and revenue Inbound and outbound differ in more ways than just their lead sourcing methods. They also take distinct approaches to targeting precision, execution complexity, and the metrics that define success. Understanding these differences can help you make smart choices about which strategy to prioritize and how much to invest. Targeting and ideal customer profile Inbound has fantastic reach but lacks the precision of outbound. Your website could receive thousands of visits per day, and your social post could reach millions of people. But the majority of them aren't going to be ideal customers. While you can certainly create digital marketing assets that attract leads with specific qualities, inbound is never as precise as outbound. In cold outreach, reps can build accurate ideal customer profiles (ICPs), generate prospecting lists of companies that align with those ICPs, and then target specific decision-makers within them. Speed and sales cycle Inbound sales is slower to generate leads than outbound sales. It typically takes longer to build awareness, trust, and purchase intent through digital marketing methods than through direct one-to-one conversations. If your offer is enticing and your messaging is highly relevant, an outbound sales approach can generate pipeline fast. In theory, you could cold call a lead one day and close the deal within a few weeks. And since you can target decision-makers directly, you can speak to people with the power to make purchases. Inbound sales, by contrast, often returns form submissions from middle managers or entry-level workers who can't purchase without first convincing their boss, which is inevitably slower than cold calling the CEO. Channels and execution complexity Inbound channels like SEO content and social media ads are generally slower to build than outbound techniques, but they have the advantage of compounding over time. They require upfront investment in content strategy, audience targeting, and technology setup, but once your campaigns and marketing assets are up and running, they tend to generate leads relatively passively. Outbound channels like email, social media, and phone are faster to activate but more labor-intensive to sustain. You can generate a prospecting list and cold-calling script in days, but if you only have 3 outbound SDRs, you can't expect to make more than 150 calls per day. Unless you're using AI tools like Artisan , scaling outbound is harder than scaling inbound. Metrics and conversion rates Inbound and outbound sales measure success differently. Typically, sales teams measure inbound effectiveness with metrics like website traffic, content engagement, and lead capture rates. These metrics track how well marketing assets and campaigns are attracting and converting leads. Sales teams measure outbound success, on the other hand, with KPIs related to sales rep activity (like calls made and emails sent) and lead responsiveness (like email reply rate and number of meetings booked). Conversion rates are usually lower for outbound since the leads don’t have any prior familiarity with or trust in your brand. But it's worth the high failure rates for those 1–3% of ideal accounts that do take a meeting. An inbound sales strategy builds demand over time Inbound sales techniques like content marketing and SEO gradually build brand awareness, create trust, and generate warm leads for your sales reps to nurture and close. Unlike outbound, which generates pipeline on demand, inbound compounds. The more helpful content you publish, the more leads come to you without further effort. Content and SEO attract qualified leads By consistently publishing genuinely helpful content, such as educational blog posts and how-to webinars, your business builds a branded library that attracts quality leads and earns trust with your target audience. With enough consistency, by the time a lead reaches out, they will already understand your offerings and believe in your business, making the job of the inbound sales rep a lot easier. If your content is evergreen and SEO-optimized, the positive effects compound. Your published materials appear in search results when leads ask relevant questions on Google, AI chatbots, and other search engines. Nurturing converts inbound leads into opportunities Once an inbound lead expresses interest and enters your sales pipeline, sales and marketing teams use lead nurturing tactics to move that lead from curious to committed. The right mix of personalized content, dispensed automatically and aligned with the lead's unique interests, guides them through the buyer's journey. The result is either a purchase or, in more complex sales, a meeting with a salesperson. The following lead nurturing tactics are among the most effective: Email marketing: Automated email sequences that deliver personalized content based on a lead's behavior and stage in the buyer's journey. Webinars: Live or on-demand videos that teach a lead how to overcome a problem while also introducing your product or service. Sales follow-ups: Automated emails, sent from a salesperson's account, that trigger when a lead takes a specified action, such as viewing a product demo or signing up for a live workshop. You can create these automated follow-ups in your CRM or AI sales tool so sales reps don't have to remember to send them. Trust is built before a salesperson steps in In inbound sales, by the time a lead speaks with a sales rep, they've likely already done lots of product research and formed opinions about your business. As a result, inbound reps can skip the introduction phase of the sales conversation and jump straight into discovery, asking questions to qualify the lead and better understand their needs. If you track how much a lead engages with your content, such as by monitoring page visits or ebook downloads, inbound sales reps can review CRM data before a discovery call or live demo. They can then come prepared with an in-depth understanding of the lead's journey, pain points, and interests. That preparation allows them to run a more personalized meeting. Outbound sales strategies create pipeline on demand A hunter has much more agency than a trap-setter. Unlike an inbound sales rep, who waits patiently for leads to come to them, an outbound seller can pick up the phone, fire off 30 cold emails, or run a multichannel sequence, generating opportunities on demand. Cold outreach targets the right people Every form of successful cold outreach starts by identifying companies that fit a well-defined ICP. From there, reps build a prospecting list of specific decision-makers, such as VPs, directors, and owners. This precise targeting delivers messages to people who have both a need for a certain solution and the power to say "yes." While you can target certain buyer personas in inbound lead generation, it's never as precise as outbound. Many low-value leads outside your ICP's parameters will fall into your funnel. With outbound, every meeting you set will be with a well-qualified lead, assuming you have the right systems in place, of course. Social selling reaches decision-makers directly Social media is another strong channel for cold outreach. Reps can directly message decision-makers, comment on their posts, and post thought leadership content that appears in their newsfeeds. This approach extends reach beyond the inbox, where prospects may already receive dozens of cold emails per day. Social selling allows you to appear on a decision-maker's radar quickly and start building a relationship. When you finally make your pitch and ask for a sales meeting, they'll be familiar with you as a person. That rapport can do wonders for conversion rates. Multi-channel sequences improve response rates The multi-channel sequence is one of the most effective and widely used outbound strategies around. This is a 7- to 14-day cadence of sales messages spread across email, phone, and social media. Here's an example of a multi-channel sequence: Day 1: Email and social media connection request Day 3: Cold call Day 6: Follow-up email Day 10: Follow-up email and social media message Day 14: Follow-up email and call This approach works because it engages leads in multiple places, which increases the chances of winning their attention. In fact, in a study of 100,000 sales campaigns , Apollo found that multi-channel campaigns using auto-email and social media produced a 14% increase in booked meetings compared to single-channel campaigns that only used auto-email. Why execution is where most outbound fails Despite its effectiveness, outbound is hard to get right. Its success is often limited by manual prospecting, poor-quality contact data, ineffective messaging, and inconsistent follow-ups. It's also difficult to scale. To boost outreach volume, most companies make the mistake of hiring more entry-level sales reps rather than investing in time-saving automation and technology. Fortunately, AI tools help solve these problems while making your outbound sales strategy far more scalable. Artisan is one example. It's an AI outbound platform that comes with an AI BDR called Ava that automates prospecting, lead enrichment, and multichannel outreach. When to use inbound vs outbound sales The right sales approach depends on how quickly you need to generate leads and whether your target audience is already looking for what you sell. In most cases, businesses don't choose one or the other. Instead, they use inbound to capture demand and outbound to create it. Why inbound works when demand already exists Inbound is most effective in markets where buyers are already searching for solutions like yours. They’re likely to find your online content and respond positively to the pitches in it. It’s also a long-term play. With inbound, it takes more time to start seeing the fruits of your efforts compared to outbound. Inbound sales fits best in the following markets: Markets with high-stakes purchases: When costs are high, buyers typically research independently before talking to sales. SaaS, financial services, healthcare, and manufacturing are all examples. Established business categories: These industries have been around for a while, so prospects already Google familiar terminology like "CRM software for small businesses" and "financial advisor in Chicago." Enterprise B2B products and services: Buyers need to build trust with the company before they're open to a pitch, which often means a period of initial research. Outbound works when you need pipeline now Outbound lead generation is ideal for companies that can't wait for customers to come to them, either because they need to generate pipeline ASAP or because they're launching a new business or product that people are unlikely to search for online. Outbound also puts you in control of timing, letting you engage potential buyers before they've started searching. Outbound works best in the following situations: Launching new products: When you're introducing something the market doesn't know to search for yet, outbound puts it in front of the right leads immediately. Entering new markets: Breaking into a new industry or region means starting from zero brand awareness. Outbound is a quick way to gain attention and avoid being crowded out by established competitors who already have a presence online. Focusing on account-based targeting: If you have a list of high-value accounts you want to reach, outbound lets you target them directly. Most B2B sales teams combine both To make sure they're reaching all potential leads, most B2B sales teams run hybrid approaches that include both inbound and outbound. They use inbound to attract and nurture contacts already in research mode while building long-term brand authority and a digital presence. In addition, they run outbound to proactively target high-value prospects and leads who may not actively be searching for their solution but would benefit from it nonetheless. For example, at Artisan, we publish SEO blog posts and social media content, but we also perform cold outreach via email and social media. Or to be more accurate, our AI BDR Ava does the outreach for us. Three common mistakes that slow down growth There are many mistakes that can cause your sales team to lose leads, waste time, and miss out on revenue. The cause is usually either overreliance on a single channel or poor strategic execution. Relying only on inbound traffic Relying on inbound leads alone is almost like going to a trade show, setting up a booth, wearing a stylish suit, and hoping people stop by. Some will trickle in, no doubt. But you have no control over the booth's performance. The most successful brands create an inviting booth, but they also send salespeople out to find potential leads, start conversations, and draw people into the booth to watch the demo and learn more. In the same way, outbound gives you much-needed control over pipeline growth. For all you know, one well-placed cold call could generate six figures in annual recurring revenue (ARR). Doing outbound without clear targeting Running outbound sales with a weak or overly broad ICP can destroy conversion rates. When your target audience is too broadly defined, it's impossible to create highly relevant messaging, which means your cold outreach is more likely to be ignored. If I were to target all restaurants in the world, instead of restaurants in New York with Google ratings of 3.5 or lower, I'd almost certainly generate little to no interest. But if I made a list of 500 similar restaurants in the same city, there’s a strong likelihood they would share goals, pain points, and challenges. That's a much easier place to start when crafting outbound messaging. I could write a single cold email sequence that resonates with every one of those business owners. The results would be more booked meetings and fewer potential leads annoyed at my irrelevant, generic emails. Scaling outbound with more people instead of better systems The old way to scale outbound was to hire more SDRs. The problem is that sales reps cost a pretty penny, and if your outbound workflows are inefficient, adding more headcount won't fix them. If sales reps were drafting emails from scratch, forgetting to follow up, and using untested scripts, adding more people just compounds these issues. Most B2B sales teams will see far better results from improving, or better yet automating, their outbound workflows with modern technology. Artisan, for example, reaches out to decision-makers with deeply personalized messages on email and social media and books meetings on autopilot. This allows you to multiply outreach volume without increasing the size of your team. Combining inbound and outbound into one system Running inbound and outbound in parallel creates a feedback loop where each method constantly sharpens the other. Inbound behavioral data helps you refine your outbound messaging, while real-time outbound conversations give you qualitative insights to shape customer-facing campaigns. Inbound data improves outbound targeting One of the best arguments for using inbound sales tactics like content marketing and advertising is that you acquire a lot of behavioral data about your customers, such as page visits, email open rates, and likes on social posts. This intel helps you understand your audience at a deeper level and identify messaging that inspires them to take action. This, in turn, helps you create more resonant outbound scripts, emails, and pitches. Inbound data also helps you refine your ICP. You might think you know who your ideal customers are, but you never know for sure until you put something online and see who visits and converts. For example, imagine you start posting marketing content on social media and discover that the users interacting most frequently are not VPs of Finance but compliance managers in tech. Now you've identified a new audience segment to target. Outbound insights improve marketing strategy Just as inbound data informs outbound strategy, outbound insights help you refine your inbound marketing. When I was an SDR doing cold calling, my benevolent manager told me that, even if I failed to book a meeting on a call, I had still succeeded as long as I learned something about the customer. The outbound rep is both a hunter and a scout. Real conversations with leads and prospects reveal pain points. Your marketing team can use these pain points to create more effective marketing campaigns, sales pages, and webinars. How automation connects the full sales process When you run inbound and outbound in parallel, there are lots of moving parts to track and weave together into a cohesive sales process. Automation tools help by ensuring that outreach, follow-up, and CRM workflows never operate in silos. Each lead action triggers the next. For example, if a lead replies to an outbound email, that signal should update the CRM status, notify the sales rep, and launch a relevant nurturing campaign. That way, no leads fall through the cracks, and they each receive the right marketing and sales touches at the right time. Many B2B teams are using Artisan to streamline and connect sales activities in exactly this way. Ava, an AI BDR around whom the platform is built, can automatically handle sequencing and personalized outreach without human intervention. She generates leads on autopilot while your sales team focuses on talking to high-intent prospects. The best sales teams don't choose a channel; they build a system If you look at the most successful B2B brands, you'll find they rarely rely on a single channel. They combine outbound methods like cold calling with inbound tactics like content marketing. To pull off this hybrid approach without introducing too much operational complexity, the right tech stack is key. With Artisan, you can automate 80% of your outbound sales. AI BDR Ava will prospect leads using a database of over 300 million decision-makers, run multi-channel sequences (including follow-ups), and book meetings. That's how you make outbound as scalable and passive as inbound without sacrificing personalization. Automate your outbound with an AI BDR Meet Ava—your AI BDR who handles prospecting, outreach, and follow-ups, so your team can focus on closing.

title: Opus Genetics Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter 2026 and Provides Corporate Update
summary: August 06, 2026 7:00am EDT - OPGx-BEST1 Cohort 1 Topline Data Expected in Second Week of September 2026 Enrollment Completed in LCA5 Registrational Trial with Dosing Planned…
body_text: Opus Genetics Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter 2026 and Provides Corporate Update August 06, 2026 7:00am EDT OPGx-BEST1 Cohort 1 Topline Data Expected in Second Week of September 2026 Enrollment Completed in LCA5 Registrational Trial with Dosing Planned for Q4 2026 RDH12, MERTK and RHO Programs Advancing with Upcoming Initiation of Clinical Testing Cash Runway into 2029 Expected to Support Multiple Clinical Inflection Points and Opportunities for Priority Review Vouchers RESEARCH TRIANGLE PARK, N.C., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Opus Genetics, Inc. (Nasdaq: IRD) (the “Company” or “Opus Genetics”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing gene therapies to restore vision and prevent blindness in patients with inherited retinal diseases (IRDs), today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided a corporate update. “With a focus on execution, we are rapidly advancing five gene therapy programs that address significant unmet need in inherited retinal diseases, with OPGx-BEST1 Cohort 1 clinical data targeted for the second week of September and four additional clinical readouts expected in 2027,” said George Magrath, M.D., Chief Executive Officer of Opus Genetics. “Based on recent FDA interactions, we finalized the OPGx-LCA5 registrational trial design. We have completed enrollment and expect to initiate participant dosing in the fourth quarter of this year. Our recent R&D Science Forum highlighted the significant progress we have made in advancing our pipeline. Our strong cash runway into 2029 positions us to initiate new clinical studies, deliver multiple data inflection points, pursue potential product approvals, and unlock opportunities for Priority Review Vouchers.” Pipeline Updates OPGx-BEST1 Enrollment was completed in Cohort 1 of the Phase 1/2 trial (BIRD-1), with 3-month topline data from Cohort 1 expected during the second week of September 2026, assuming all participants complete their assessments as scheduled. Baseline demographics were presented at the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology (ARVO) 2026 Annual Meeting with the related poster presentation available on the Publications & Presentations page of the Opus Genetics website. Additionally, a slide presentation and video summary recording titled “OPGx-BEST1 Cohort 1 Baseline Demographics and Key Endpoints for IRDs” are provided on the OPGx-BEST1 Program section of the Opus Genetics website. OPGx-LCA5 Alignment was achieved with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the registrational Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating OPGx-LCA5 in eight participants with a six-month run-in period, allowing each participant to serve as their own control, prior to receiving treatment in both eyes. Enrollment in the trial was completed, with dosing of OPGx-LCA5 expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026 using clinical drug supply manufactured with the intended commercial processes. Topline data from the study is expected by the end of 2027. OPGx-RDH12 The OPGx-RDH12 program is expected to enter the clinic in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is partially funded through a partnership with the RDH12 Alliance. OPGx-MERTK The OPGx-MERTK program is expected to initiate clinical testing at the Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi in the first quarter of 2027. OPGx-RHO Preclinical data presented at ARVO 2026 and the Foundation Fighting Blindness Retinal Therapeutics Innovation Summit 2026 provided safety and efficacy data on the use of OPGx-RHO in two large animal models of autosomal-dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP). The OPGx-RHO program is expected to initiate clinical testing globally in the second half of 2027. Recent Medical Presentations Opus Genetics delivered numerous data presentations at prominent medical meetings during the period including at the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology (ARVO), Retina World Congress, and the American Society of Gene & Cell Therapy. In addition, in July 2026, Human Gene Therapy published “Evaluation of the Toxicity and Efficacy of an Adeno‑Associated Viral Vector Expressing BEST1 Delivered by Subretinal Injection in a Canine Model of Human Bestrophinopathy”. All materials can be found on the Publications & Presentations page of the Company website. Financial Results for the Second Quarter Ended June 30, 2026 Cash Position : As of June 30, 2026, Opus Genetics had cash and cash equivalents of $88.8 million. With the current cash and cash equivalents, and potential future fundings under the note purchase agreement with Oberland Capital Management, the Company believes its aggregate cash resources will fund operations into 2029. This estimate excludes any potential proceeds from callable warrants or future milestone payments. Revenue : License and collaborations revenue totaled $0.8 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $2.9 million for the same period in 2025. Revenue in both periods came primarily from reimbursement of research and development (R&D) services based on the Company’s collaboration with Viatris, Inc. Research and Development (R&D) Expenses: R&D expenses were $11.2 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $6.0 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primar ily attributable to higher manufacturing and clinical costs associated with the Company's IRD programs, partially offset by lower clinical costs associated with the Phentolamine Ophthalmic Solution 0.75% programs. Research and development expenses included $0.4 million and $0.3 million in stock-based compensation expense for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. General and Administrative (G&A) Expenses: G&A expenses were $6.0 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $5.8 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher employee compensation costs, partially offset by lower public company related costs. General and administrative expenses included $1.0 million and $0.6 million in stock-based compensation expense during the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. title: Amazon celebra el primer aniversario de la reapertura de sus tours en España con más de 8.000 visitantes
summary: Durante los últimos doce meses, la compañía ha organizado más de 600 visitas a sus centros logísticos de Illescas (Toledo) y El Prat de Llobregat (Barcelona).Estos tours gratuitos permiten conocer de primera mano las personas, la tecnología y los procesos que hacen posible las operaciones de Amazon.
body_text: Durante los últimos doce meses, la compañía ha organizado más de 600 visitas a sus centros logísticos de Illescas (Toledo) y El Prat de Llobregat (Barcelona). Estos tours gratuitos permiten conocer de primera mano las personas, la tecnología y los procesos que hacen posible las operaciones de Amazon. 05/08/2026 | Madrid Amazon celebra el primer aniversario de la reapertura de sus tours presenciales en España, una iniciativa que permite acercar sus operaciones al público y conocer, de primera mano, cómo funcionan sus centros logísticos. Desde su reanudación hace un año, la compañía ha organizado más de 600 tours, en los que han participado más de 8.000 personas. Actualmente, Amazon ofrece estas visitas presenciales en sus centros logísticos de Illescas (Toledo) y El Prat de Llobregat (Barcelona). Los tours son gratuitos, tienen una duración aproximada de entre 60 y 90 minutos y permiten a los participantes conocer el recorrido que realizan los productos dentro de las instalaciones, así como las personas, la tecnología y los procesos que hacen posible la preparación de los pedidos de los clientes. Esta acogida refleja el interés por conocer las operaciones de Amazon desde dentro. Durante el recorrido, los visitantes pueden observar diferentes áreas de las instalaciones y descubrir algunas de las tecnologías empleadas en ellas, incluidos los sistemas de robótica y las cintas transportadoras que contribuyen al movimiento de los productos a lo largo de las distintas fases del proceso logístico. En el año en que Amazon celebra su 15 aniversario en España, esta experiencia permite comprender también cómo la inversión en tecnología y la expansión de su red logística han contribuido a ofrecer a los clientes una selección cada vez mayor de productos y hacer posibles entregas cada vez más rápidas, incluido el mismo día o al día siguiente en 16 ciudades de España. Una experiencia para conocer las operaciones de Amazon desde dentro Las visitas están guiadas por empleados y empleadas de Amazon, que acompañan a los participantes durante el recorrido y explican el funcionamiento de las instalaciones y el papel que desempeñan los distintos equipos y tecnologías. De este modo, los tours ofrecen una visión directa de la actividad que se desarrolla diariamente en los centros logísticos y permiten comprender mejor cómo la combinación de personas, tecnología e innovación contribuye al funcionamiento de las operaciones de Amazon. "Estamos muy satisfechos con la acogida que han tenido los tours desde su reapertura hace un año. Más de 8.000 personas han visitado nuestros centros logísticos en este primer año, y eso es el mejor reflejo de la magia que se vive dentro de nuestras instalaciones. Abrir nuestras puertas permite a la gente descubrir de primera mano el trabajo de nuestros equipos y cómo la tecnología y la innovación hacen posible que cada pedido llegue a tiempo". Marco Baggio Director regional de operaciones de Amazon en España La iniciativa forma parte del compromiso de Amazon por acercar sus operaciones a las comunidades en las que está presente, ofreciendo a ciudadanos, familias y otros colectivos la posibilidad de conocer sus instalaciones y a las personas que trabajan en ellas. Los tours por los centros logísticos de Amazon son gratuitos y requieren reserva previa. Las personas interesadas pueden consultar las ubicaciones, fechas y horarios disponibles y reservar su visita a través de Amazon Tours . Sobre Amazon Amazon se guía por cuatro principios: enfoque en el consumidor por encima de la competencia, pasión por innovar, compromiso con la excelencia operativa y visión a largo plazo. Amazon se esfuerza por ser la empresa más centrada en el cliente del mundo, el mejor empleador y el lugar de trabajo más seguro del planeta. Las opiniones de los clientes, compra en 1-Clic, recomendaciones personalizadas, Prime, Logística de Amazon, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Kindle Direct Publishing, Kindle, Career Choice, Fire, Fire TV, Amazon Echo, Alexa, tecnología Just Walk Out, Amazon Studios y The Climate Pledge son algunas de las iniciativas pioneras de Amazon. Para más información, visita www.aboutamazon.es y síguenos en Twitter, @AmazonNewsES , Instagram, @amazonespana y Facebook, @AmazonEspana .

title: Samsara Launches Fuel Command Center to Help Fleets Control Costs Amid Price Volatility
summary: Samsara Launches Fuel Command Center to Help Fleets Control Costs Amid Price Volatility
body_text: Press Releases / Samsara Fuel Command Center Samsara Launches Fuel Command Center to Help Fleets Control Costs Amid Price Volatility August 19, 2026 New centralized experience brings fuel usage, driver behavior, routing, and card controls into a single pane of glass for operations and finance teams SAN FRANCISCO, August 19, 2026 — Samsara (NYSE: IOT), the pioneer of the Connected Operations® Platform, today launched the Samsara Fuel Command Center, a centralized experience that brings its fuel management capabilities into a single pane of glass. It combines a consolidated view of total and recoverable fuel spend with intelligent fuel-stop recommendations in Commercial Navigation and Coast fuel card controls, giving operations and finance teams one place to identify waste, guide drivers to lower-cost fuel, and prevent card misuse. “We used to worry about fraud all the time. Cards went missing, PINs were shared, and we had no way to verify transactions,” said Tim Weisser, Fleet Operations Manager at Milestone Home Services. "Now with Coast and Samsara, the system takes care of it. If the truck's not there, the card doesn't work. Simple.” Commercial fleets have contended with sustained fuel misuse and price volatility throughout 2026, as diesel prices have moved by more than $0.20 per gallon in a single week seven times since late February, according to data from the Samsara Fuel Spend Index . The latest swing erased three consecutive months of declines in just four weeks, pushing diesel to $5.23 per gallon by the end of July—16% above where the month began—while gasoline climbed from $3.93 to $4.25. This unpredictability heightens the need for cost controls and presents a significant opportunity. Internal data shows that U.S. customers had roughly $2 billion in potential fuel-spend savings in the first six months of the year. The Fuel Command Center gives operators the tools to capture those savings as conditions change. “Fuel is one of the biggest costs a fleet carries— 30% to 40% of total marginal operating costs,” said Ryan Yu, VP of Product at Samsara. “Prices have swung hard the past several months, and when they rise, fuel fraud rises with them. Customers told us pump-price visibility isn't enough. They need fraud, driver behavior, and vendor choices in one view, so they can cut costs before they add up. That's why we built Fuel Command Center: to give operators and finance leaders a way to turn their operations data into action and find immediate savings.” The Fuel Command Center centralizes the data and controls fleets use to manage fuel across three core areas: See total and recoverable fuel spend in one place Fuel Command Center gives operations and finance teams a consolidated view of total and recoverable fuel spend. It identifies where money is being lost across idling, fueling location, driver efficiency, fraud, and suspicious fuel drops, then recommends the highest-impact actions. Managers can track quarterly trends and act from the same dashboard—for example, by turning on in-cab idling alerts or adding preferred fuel vendors. Route drivers to the right fuel stop with Commercial Navigation Commercial Navigation extends the centralized fuel strategy to the road by building preferred fuel stops into a route before a driver leaves the yard, so drivers do not have to toggle between telematics and third-party fuel apps. It accounts for corporate negotiated rates, responds when fuel runs low mid-route, and reroutes to the nearest preferred station. In a 90-day analysis of more than 2,000 Samsara customers, organizations cut a median of 4% in fuel spend by fueling at preferred vendors. Stop card misuse before the transaction with Coast Fuel card misuse rises with fuel prices: a Samsara analysis found that detected fraud incidents increase roughly 9% for every $0.10 increase in the price of diesel. Through the Samsara Coast integration , Fuel Command Center connects card authorization to vehicle location, allowing fleets to manage policies in one place and block transactions when the assigned vehicle is not present. “After implementing Coast through Samsara, we saw our fuel expenses drop by nearly $15,000 a month,” said Kyle Stewart, CFO at Trades Holding. While fleets cannot control the price of fuel, they can control more of what they ultimately spend, and by centralizing fuel performance, routing, driver behavior, and card controls in Fuel Command Center, Samsara gives operations and finance teams one place to manage the variables that determine that cost. The result is a more direct way to offset external price volatility with savings generated inside their own operations. Learn more about Samsara’s Fuel Command Center here . Learn more about Samsara’s Commercial Navigation here . Learn more about the Samsara and Coast integration here . Explore current Samsara Fuel Spend Index data here. Read about 8 ways to manage surging fuel costs here . About Samsara Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations® Platform, which is an open platform that connects the people, devices, and systems of some of the world's most complex operations, allowing them to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. With tens of thousands of customers across North America and Europe, Samsara is a proud technology partner to the people who keep our global economy running, including the world's leading organizations across industries in transportation, construction, wholesale and retail trade, field services, logistics, manufacturing, utilities and energy, government, healthcare and education, food and beverage, and others. The company's mission is to increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of the operations that power the global economy. Samsara is a registered trademark of Samsara Inc.
