title: Accounts Receivable Software: 8 Tools Compared for 2026
summary: Eight accounts receivable software tools compared Finlens, QuickBooks Online, Xero, Wave, Zoho Invoice, Bill.com, Upflow, FreshBooks. Verdict per vendor, decision framework, and where each tool breaks.
body_text: The best accounts receivable software depends on invoice volume, whether AR needs to reconcile to a full general ledger, and how much billing complexity you carry. For businesses without existing bookkeeping software, Finlens built for accounting firms and small businesses runs AR inside a full accounting ledger with automated categorization and close. QuickBooks Online and Xero cover most growing small businesses with built-in AR. Wave and Zoho Invoice cover freelancers on free tiers. Bill.com and Upflow are dedicated AR automation for B2B businesses that have outgrown accounting-native AR. FreshBooks sits between invoicing and full accounting. Key takeaways The AR software market splits into three categories invoicing-only, accounting with built-in AR, and dedicated AR automation and choosing category matters more than choosing specific tool. Median US B2B Days Sales Outstanding sits at ~40 days according to Atradius Payment Practices Barometer and Investopedia's DSO explainer ; automated reminders plus online payment acceptance typically drop DSO by 5–15 days. Standard overdue escalation cadence is 7 / 14 / 21 / 30 days past due, with reminders escalating from friendly nudge to personal outreach. Fix internal process gaps missing POs, disputes, wrong billing contact before adding more automation; ~40% of "late payments" trace to internal breakdowns, not truly late payers. Finlens runs full AR inside a standalone accounting platform invoice creation, aging, reminder cadence, cash application, and ledger reconciliation in one system, with a free tier for small businesses that don't have QuickBooks or Xero yet. Best accounts receivable software: comparison table # Vendor One-line verdict Best for Starting price 1 Finlens Standalone AR + full accounting ledger with automated categorization Small businesses and CAS firms wanting AR + close in one system Free tier; paid from custom 2 QuickBooks Online Category default for SMB accounting with built-in AR Growing small businesses already on QBO $35/mo Simple Start 3 Xero Alternative SMB accounting with strong AR + international support Small businesses outside US or with international billing $20/mo Early 4 Wave Free invoicing with basic AR; reminders often behind paid tier Freelancers and micro-businesses invoicing occasionally Free; Pro $16/mo 5 Zoho Invoice Free tier includes automated reminders and 1,000 invoices/year Solo operators wanting reminders without a paid tier Free 6 Bill.com Dedicated AP/AR automation sitting on top of accounting software Mid-market businesses with high invoice volume $45/user/mo 7 Upflow B2B AR automation focused on collections and cash application B2B SaaS with complex billing and heavy collections load Custom 8 FreshBooks Invoicing-first with lightweight accounting features Service businesses and consultants with simple books $19/mo Lite Pricing reflects published starting tiers early 2026 and does not include add-ons or per-invoice fees. The 8 best accounts receivable software tools 1. Finlens Overview. Finlens is a standalone AI-native accounting platform with accounts receivable, month-end close, categorization, and multi-client reconciliation built in. For small businesses without existing bookkeeping software, AR runs directly inside Finlens; for accounting firms and CAS providers , same AR workflow runs across an entire book of clients from one dashboard. Best for. Small businesses that don't want to route through QuickBooks or Xero to get modern AR. CAS firms serving many clients on recurring engagements who need AR tied to a full close pack every month with predictable pricing tiers for staff time. Key features. Invoice generation with recurring schedules, configurable reminder cadence (7 / 14 / 21 / 30 days), AR aging by client, automated cash application, tamper-evident audit log, multi-client exception review, and reconciliation to general ledger. Free tier available for small businesses. Pricing. Free tier for small business use. Paid tiers custom-quoted for CAS firms and higher-volume books. Limitations. Not a dedicated collections platform Bill.com and Upflow have deeper deduction-management and credit-scoring features for enterprise B2B. Not a fit for a business that only needs standalone invoicing with no accounting. Where it breaks. High-volume enterprise B2B AR with complex deduction management. That workload belongs on a dedicated AR platform sitting on top of a general ledger. 2. QuickBooks Online Overview. QuickBooks Online is category default for US small-business accounting, and AR is one of its native modules. According to G2's accounting software category data , QuickBooks retains largest installed base of any US small-business accounting product. A user on r/Entrepreneurs described it as reliable choice "for invoices/bookkeeping" when business already runs on QBO. Best for. Growing US small businesses already on QuickBooks Online who want AR inside same system as everything else. Key features. Invoice templates, recurring invoices, automated payment reminders (Essentials tier and above), online payment acceptance via QuickBooks Payments, AR aging reports, and cash application to ledger. Pricing. $35/mo Simple Start · $65 Essentials · $99 Plus · $235 Advanced. Limitations. Automated reminders and multi-user access are gated behind Essentials or higher. Payment processing fees are separate. Complex billing (usage-based, multi-tier) hits limits. Where it breaks. Multi-entity billing, high invoice volume above ~500/month, and B2B collections workflows with heavy dispute handling. 3. Xero Overview. Xero is international counterpart to QuickBooks full small-business accounting with AR built in. Particularly strong outside US and for businesses with international billing. Best for. Small businesses outside US market, multi-currency AR, and businesses whose accountants prefer Xero to QuickBooks. Key features. Invoice creation with online payment links, automated invoice reminders, AR aging, multi-currency support at standard tier, and native reconciliation to general ledger. Pricing. $20/mo Early · $47 Growing · $80 Established. Limitations. Early tier caps invoices sent at 20 per month and bill entry at 5 per month. Payroll requires Gusto or a separate add-on in US. Reporting is less deep than QuickBooks Advanced. Where it breaks. US businesses whose accounting firm exclusively works in QuickBooks; heavy inventory-plus-AR workflows. 4. Wave Overview. Wave is free-tier default for freelancers and micro-businesses who need to send invoices and track basic AR without paying for software. A commenter on r/smallbusiness put it plainly: "Free plan on Wave is unlimited invoicing but reminders are manual otherwise." Best for. Solo operators and freelancers invoicing occasionally who want free invoicing and basic bookkeeping. Key features. Unlimited invoicing (free), online payment acceptance, receipt scanning, basic accounting, and one bank account connection on free tier. Pricing. Free (Starter) · Pro $16/mo. Payment processing fees separate. Limitations. Automated invoice reminders require Pro tier or enabling online payments. AR aging reports are basic. No inventory. Limited integration ecosystem. Where it breaks. Any business past 20–30 invoices a month or needing multi-user access. 5. Zoho Invoice Overview. Zoho Invoice is outlier free tier a free invoicing tool that includes automated reminders and up to 1,000 invoices per year without a gotcha, described on r/smallbusiness as "worth a look specifically because it includes automated reminders with no gotcha." Best for. Solo operators and micro-businesses wanting free automated reminders without a paid tier. Key features. Invoice creation with 1,000 invoices/year, automated payment reminders on custom schedules, online payment acceptance, expense tracking, and time tracking. Integrates with Zoho Books for full accounting. Pricing. Free (up to 1,000 invoices/year). Limitations. Not full accounting Zoho Books ($15/mo+) is upgrade path. Limited customization on free tier. Interface less polished than paid competitors. Where it breaks. Businesses past 1,000 invoices/year or needing full general-ledger accounting. 6. Bill.com Overview. Bill.com is dedicated AP and AR automation that sits on top of an existing accounting system QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, or Sage Intacct. It handles invoice creation, approval workflows, and payment collection at scale. Best for. Mid-market businesses with high invoice volume, multi-approver workflows, and an existing accounting system they don't want to replace. Key features. Invoice creation and delivery, custom approval routing, payment collection (ACH, credit card, check), integration with QuickBooks / Xero / NetSuite / Sage Intacct, and audit trail. Pricing. $45/user/mo Essentials · $55 Team · $79 Corporate · custom Enterprise. Limitations. Not a standalone ledger requires an accounting system underneath. Per-user pricing scales quickly for larger teams. Some workflow customization requires higher tiers. Where it breaks. Small businesses without an existing accounting system; usage-based billing that needs deep CPQ. 7. Upflow Overview. Upflow is dedicated B2B AR automation focused on collections side smart reminder sequences, customer portals, and cash application. A commenter on r/AccountingDepartment noted researching Upflow specifically for B2B SaaS AR automation. Best for. B2B SaaS and growing services businesses with a real collections load complex billing arrangements, DSO problems, and a finance team ready to invest in dedicated collections tooling. Key features. Automated collections workflows, customer AR portals, cash application, DSO analytics, and native integrations with QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, and Stripe. Pricing. Custom (typically starts around $500+/mo). Limitations. Not a general ledger sits on top of accounting software. Small-business scale rarely justifies price. Where it breaks. Solo operators, freelancers, and any business without a dedicated collections need. 8. FreshBooks Overview. FreshBooks sits between an invoicing tool and a full accounting system invoicing-first with lightweight accounting features layered on. Popular with service businesses and consultants who need cleaner invoicing than a spreadsheet without depth of QuickBooks. Best for. Service businesses, consultants, and small agencies invoicing time-and-materials or fixed-fee retainers. Key features. Invoice templates, recurring invoices, time tracking, expense tracking, automated late-payment reminders, online payments, and a project-based billing view. Pricing. $19/mo Lite · $33 Plus · $60 Premium · custom Select. Limitations. Lite tier caps at 5 billable clients. Accounting features are lighter than QuickBooks or Xero. Not designed for inventory or high-transaction-volume books. Where it breaks. Product-based businesses with inventory; businesses needing multi-currency reporting or heavy financial customization. Which accounts receivable software should you choose The right tool depends on invoice volume, billing complexity, and whether AR needs to reconcile to a full general ledger. Use this decision framework: Use Finlens if you're a small business without existing bookkeeping software or a CAS firm managing AR across many clients and you want AR, close, and reconciliation in one system with a free tier for SMB use case. Use QuickBooks Online if you're already on QuickBooks and need AR inside same ledger you already run everything else through. Use Xero if you're outside US, have multi-currency AR, or your accountant works exclusively in Xero. Use Wave if you're a freelancer invoicing occasionally and free is more important than automated reminders. Use Zoho Invoice if you want automated reminders on a free tier and you're under 1,000 invoices a year. Use Bill.com if you're mid-market with high invoice volume and an existing accounting system you don't want to replace. Use Upflow if you're a B2B business with real collections load, complex billing, and a finance team ready to invest in dedicated AR tooling. Use FreshBooks if you're a service business or consultant and invoicing polish matters more than accounting depth. A practitioner heuristic from r/AccountingDepartment that keeps coming up: "Most AR delays aren't actually 'late payers' it's internal breakdowns: missing / incorrect POs, disputes sitting unresolved." Fix those before shopping for more automation. The U.S. Small Business Administration guide on managing finances is a good starting reference on invoicing terms and getting paid faster. Common AR software integrations AR software rarely lives alone. Real workflows depend on integrations: Payment processors Stripe, ACH via Plaid, credit card gateways. Native payment acceptance on invoice itself materially improves paid-in-full rates. Accounting systems bidirectional sync with QuickBooks, Xero, or business's primary ledger so AR balance and GL agree at month-end. See our guide on QuickBooks automation for what "good sync" actually looks like. CRM customer records flow from Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive into invoice recipients. Communication channels email plus, increasingly, SMS reminders for oldest overdue balances. One user on r/smallbusiness reported: "switching to SMS follow up instead of email for overdue invoices. response rate is completely different." An "accounting@" shared inbox for reminders described on r/smallbusiness as helping reminders "feel procedural rather than personal" is a cheap process improvement most businesses can adopt on day one, regardless of tool. A contributor on r/Bookkeeping noted that most modern platforms let you set an escalation schedule as "a rule and forget it," so manual chase is a workflow choice, not a tool constraint. Conclusion The right accounts receivable software depends on invoice volume, billing complexity, and whether AR needs to reconcile to a full general ledger not on brand recognition. Most small businesses land on accounting software with built-in AR. Freelancers use free-tier invoicing tools. B2B mid-market graduates to dedicated AR automation. Book a 20-minute walkthrough with Finlens if AR is where cash is currently getting stuck bring one month's aging report and we'll show you where automation replaces manual chase, whether Finlens runs as your ledger or on top of an existing one. FAQ What is accounts receivable software? Accounts receivable software is a system that automates invoicing, payment reminders, aging tracking, and cash application. It manages money customers owe from invoice creation through payment collection and reconciliation to general ledger. What is best accounts receivable software for small business? QuickBooks Online and Xero are category defaults for growing small businesses. Wave and Zoho Invoice are best free options. Finlens is standalone-accounting option for small businesses that don't have QuickBooks or Xero yet, with a free tier. Is accounts receivable software same as invoicing software? No invoicing software is a subset. Invoicing software creates and sends invoices; accounts receivable software adds aging tracking, automated reminders, cash application, dispute handling, and reconciliation to general ledger. Every AR system includes invoicing; not every invoicing tool covers full AR. How much does accounts receivable software cost? Free tiers exist (Wave, Zoho Invoice). Accounting software with built-in AR runs $20–$100/month (QuickBooks, Xero, pricing tier ranges ). Dedicated AR automation platforms like Bill.com start around $45/user/month; Upflow and other B2B-focused platforms start around $500/month. What is DSO in accounts receivable? DSO stands for Days Sales Outstanding average number of days it takes to collect payment after a sale. The US median for B2B businesses is around 40 days per Atradius. Automated reminders plus online payment acceptance typically drop DSO by 5–15 days. Do I need accounts receivable software if I have accounting software? Usually not. Modern accounting software includes AR functionality. A separate AR platform makes sense only if invoice volume, dispute rates, or billing complexity outgrow what accounting-native AR can handle. Can Finlens replace QuickBooks for accounts receivable? Yes for small businesses without existing bookkeeping Finlens is a full standalone accounting platform with AR built in. For businesses already on QuickBooks, Finlens automates categorization, close, and multi-client reconciliation on top of QuickBooks rather than replacing it. What features should I look for in accounts receivable software? The essentials are invoice templates, automated payment reminders on a defined schedule (7 / 14 / 21 / 30 days is standard), online payment acceptance, AR aging reports, cash application matching payments to invoices, and reconciliation to general ledger. At larger scale, add dispute management, credit memos, and DSO reporting.

title: 9 Top Rated AI Sales Assistants to Demo in 2026
summary: Find the right AI sales assistant for your team. Compare nine leading AI-powered sales platforms based on features, pricing, strengths, and limitations.
body_text: Sales reps rarely spend their entire day selling. Most of the work happens before and after every conversation. Prospect research, CRM updates, writing follow up emails, scheduling meetings, updating opportunity stages, looking for buying signals, and keeping dozens of conversations moving all compete for attention. Before long, selling becomes one task squeezed between a long list of administrative responsibilities. Recent workplace research paints a familiar picture. Office professionals lose more than an hour every day completing repetitive administrative work that artificial intelligence could handle. Email alone consumes well over four hours during an average workday for many professionals. For sales teams juggling dozens of active prospects, those hours add up quickly. This growing workload explains why AI sales assistants have become one of the fastest growing software categories in revenue technology. These platforms are not trying to replace salespeople. Good sales conversations still depend on trust, curiosity, timing, and experience. No software can replicate the judgment that helps a salesperson handle objections, uncover buying motives, or recognize when a prospect is ready to move forward. What modern AI powered sales copilots can do remarkably well is remove everything surrounding those conversations. They can research prospects before the first outreach, draft personalized follow ups after meetings, summarize calls, update CRM records, surface buying signals, recommend next actions, and keep opportunities moving without forcing reps to spend their evenings catching up on administrative work. Every hour saved becomes another hour available for prospecting, discovery calls, demos, or customer conversations. Also Read: 10 Super Powerful AI Sales Assistant Platforms in 2026 (Expert Review) 9 Best AI Based Sales Assistants for 2026 that Pack a Punch Best AI Sales Assistants That simple value proposition explains why sales organizations of every size are beginning to evaluate Intelligent sales assistant software alongside traditional CRMs and sales engagement platforms. AI Sales Assistants Are Solving Two Very Different Problems One reason buyers become confused is because almost every vendor now markets itself as an AI sales assistant. The category has grown far beyond simple email writers. Today there are two very different groups of products. The first group focuses on filling your pipeline. These products help sales development representatives identify prospects, enrich contact data, personalize outreach, launch multi touch campaigns, and book first meetings. Platforms like Apollo.io, Cognism, and outbound focused sales engagement systems belong here. The second group focuses on helping salespeople after conversations begin. These products summarize meetings, prepare follow ups, capture CRM notes, recommend next steps, provide coaching during calls, and organize pipeline activity automatically. They spend less time helping you find prospects and far more time helping you convert opportunities into revenue. Many organizations eventually adopt both categories. One helps generate conversations. The other helps move those conversations toward closed business. If you're asking What are the best AI sales assistants to demo in 2026? , the answer depends heavily on where your team spends the most time every week. Teams struggling with outbound prospecting will prioritize one type of platform. Teams overwhelmed with administrative work after meetings will often see faster returns from another. How We Evaluated These AI Sales Assistants Marketing pages make every platform sound revolutionary. Every vendor promises automation, productivity improvements, intelligent recommendations, and personalized outreach. Daily usage tells a much different story. To separate useful software from impressive marketing, every product on this list was evaluated during two weeks of realistic sales activity. Prospect research, outbound sequences, discovery calls, follow up emails, CRM updates, and meeting preparation all became part of the evaluation process. Several products performed well in one area while creating unnecessary friction somewhere else. Others looked simple at first but quietly removed hours of repetitive work every week. These were the five areas that mattered most. Removes Administrative Work Instead of Simply Helping With It Many products describe themselves as AI assistants. Some simply generate content after you click a button. Others complete the work with very little involvement from the salesperson. That difference matters. Writing an email draft saves a few minutes. Preparing the follow up, updating CRM fields, scheduling the next task, logging meeting notes, and surfacing buying signals without constant prompting creates a much larger productivity gain. The best Automated sales task and workflow assistants quietly complete repetitive work while the rep stays focused on customer conversations. Fits Naturally Into Existing Sales Workflows Sales teams already live inside several different systems every day. Email. CRM. Calendar. Sales engagement platforms. Calling software. Meeting tools. Adding another isolated application rarely improves productivity. The platforms earning higher scores integrated naturally with existing workflows. Reps spent more time selling and less time switching between browser tabs. This also answers one of the most common buying questions: Which AI sales assistants integrate with your existing sales engagement platform? Products supporting major ecosystems such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and popular dialers naturally ranked much higher. Works Across Gmail and Outlook Many vendors quietly prioritize Gmail while offering limited Outlook support. Large enterprise organizations continue running Microsoft environments, while startups often live entirely inside Google Workspace. Compatibility across both ecosystems reduces deployment headaches and allows mixed sales organizations to standardize on one platform. Produces Output That Sounds Human Prospects immediately recognize generic AI writing. Follow ups filled with corporate clichés rarely receive replies. Every drafting feature was evaluated for personalization, context awareness, conversational flow, and writing quality. Good AI powered sales copilots should sound like experienced salespeople who understand previous conversations. They should never sound like a template generated five seconds ago. Honest About Product Limitations No software solves every problem. Some tools specialize in prospecting ; others focus on coaching. Those limitations deserve as much attention as feature lists because they determine long term adoption inside a sales organization. Software Best For Core AI Strength Starting Price CRM Support Key Limitation Apollo.io Prospecting AI outreach, prospect database, buying intent, enrichment, sequencing Free $49/user/mo Salesforce HubSpot Pipedrive Limited post-meeting productivity and coaching Trellus Outbound SDRs AI coaching, parallel dialing, research, follow-ups, workflow automation Contact Sales Popular CRMs Best suited for outbound-focused organizations HubSpot Breeze AI HubSpot Users CRM summaries, email drafting, lead scoring, AI prospecting Sales Hub from ~$90/user/mo Native HubSpot Best inside HubSpot ecosystem Salesforce Agentforce Enterprise Autonomous CRM actions, forecasting, opportunity intelligence Usage Based Native Salesforce Requires Salesforce administration Cognism International Prospecting GDPR data, AI account recommendations, intent signals Custom Major CRMs Limited coaching and meeting intelligence Salesken Live Coaching Real-time coaching, objection handling, conversation scoring Custom Major CRMs No prospect database Otter.ai Meeting Notes Transcription, AI summaries, searchable meetings Free Paid Plans Available Salesforce HubSpot Limited sales intelligence features tl;dv Meeting Intelligence CRM updates, AI summaries, coaching insights, conversation search Free Paid Plans Available HubSpot Salesforce Pipedrive No outbound prospect database People.ai Revenue Intelligence Activity capture, forecasting, account coverage, pipeline insights Custom Enterprise CRMs Designed for leadership rather than SDR workflows 1. Apollo.io Apollo.io continues to be one of the easiest recommendations for outbound sales teams because it combines several products that companies often purchase separately. Everything lives under one platform. Sales teams looking for an efficient way to build prospect lists, launch campaigns, and manage outbound activity can move from research to first outreach without jumping across multiple applications. Over the past couple of years the platform has expanded its artificial intelligence capabilities considerably. Users can generate sequence copy, personalize messaging around different buyer personas, receive engagement insights, and identify accounts showing buying intent. For organizations building predictable outbound pipelines, Apollo.io remains one of the more complete AI driven sales intelligence and insights platforms available today. Best For Outbound sales teams looking for prospect data, enrichment, sequencing, and personalization inside one application. Key Features Before looking at the feature list, it helps to understand why Apollo remains popular. Many competitors perform one task very well. Apollo combines several stages of prospecting inside one environment, reducing the number of separate subscriptions many sales organizations need. Large B2B contact and company database with enrichment Multi step email and calling sequences AI generated outreach personalization Buyer intent signals and job change monitoring CRM synchronization with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Pipedrive Prospect filtering using company size, technology stack, industry, revenue, and hiring activity Pricing A free plan is available with limited credits. Paid plans begin around $49 per user each month. Limitations Apollo remains heavily focused on generating pipeline. Its email writing performs well for large outbound campaigns, although experienced sellers will usually edit AI generated messages before sending them. Deliverability can also become less predictable for organizations sending extremely high volumes of outbound email. Teams looking for meeting summaries, CRM automation after sales calls, coaching, and ongoing deal management will usually pair Apollo with another platform that specializes in post meeting productivity. 2. Trellus Most AI sales assistants either help you before the conversation starts or after the meeting ends. Very few improve what happens during the conversation itself. That is where Trellus earns its place near the top of this list. The platform was built around a simple idea. Salespeople should spend less time managing technology and more time speaking with qualified prospects. Every feature supports that objective. Rather than asking reps to piece together several disconnected applications, it combines outbound calling, prospect research, AI coaching, workflow automation, and post call productivity into one workspace. For outbound teams making dozens of calls every day, those small productivity gains quickly compound. One less minute searching for account information. Another minute saved writing follow up emails. Several minutes saved updating CRM records. Multiply that across fifty or sixty conversations in a week and the time savings become meaningful. This makes it much more than another dialer with artificial intelligence attached to the product description. It functions as one of the more complete AI sales assistants for outbound sales organizations that want help before, during, and after every customer conversation. Another area where the platform stands out is context. Good conversations rarely happen because someone memorized a script. They happen because the salesperson understands the account, listens carefully, adapts naturally, and responds with confidence. The workspace brings together account research, conversation guidance, live coaching, and post call recommendations so reps spend less mental energy switching between browser tabs and more attention listening to prospects. For growing SDR teams, this also creates a valuable coaching environment. New hires receive guidance while experienced reps continue refining their conversations without managers reviewing every single recording manually. When people ask Can AI sales assistants help reps win more deals without replacing human judgment? , this is exactly the kind of platform that answers that question well. Artificial intelligence handles repetitive work. Salespeople handle relationships. That balance produces better conversations without removing the human side of selling. Best For Sales development teams and outbound organizations that want one workspace for calling, coaching, prospect research, workflow automation, and meeting generation. Key Features The platform combines several capabilities that sales teams would normally spread across multiple applications. Bringing everything together reduces context switching throughout the day while helping reps stay focused on conversations rather than administrative work. AI powered parallel dialing to increase live conversations Real time coaching during outbound calls AI generated prospect research before every conversation Personalized talking points based on account context AI practice calls for onboarding and ongoing coaching Smart voicemail drop Automatic call summaries and follow up recommendations Advanced call analytics for managers Number health monitoring to improve outbound performance CRM synchronization with popular sales platforms LinkedIn integration that keeps prospect research inside the calling workflow Several of these features work together particularly well. The salesperson can immediately move to the next conversation instead of spending fifteen minutes documenting everything that just happened. Those small workflow improvements are exactly why many organizations continue investing in Automated sales task and workflow assistants . Why It Fits This List This platform connects several of those activities into one outbound workflow, making it particularly attractive for SDR organizations where speed, consistency, and coaching all matter at the same time. It also contributes to another important question buyers frequently ask. How do AI sales assistants improve rep productivity and deal close rates? The answer usually has very little to do with replacing salespeople. Better productivity comes from reducing repetitive work. More conversations happen because preparation takes less time. Managers coach more efficiently because important moments are already highlighted. Reps spend more hours speaking with buyers instead of documenting conversations. As a result, those improvements often produce better pipeline coverage long before anyone starts measuring closed revenue. Pricing Limitations The platform delivers the greatest value for outbound organizations making high volumes of customer conversations. Companies searching exclusively for meeting transcription or CRM reporting may find more specialized products that focus entirely on those individual areas. 3. HubSpot Breeze AI HubSpot already serves as the central workspace for thousands of sales organizations. Adding artificial intelligence directly inside the CRM makes adoption much easier because salespeople do not need another application sitting beside everything else they already use. That is the biggest advantage of HubSpot Breeze AI. Rather than introducing a completely separate assistant, the intelligence appears throughout the CRM where salespeople already spend their day. Opportunity records, emails, contacts, tasks, and pipeline updates all become smarter without forcing users to learn an entirely new workflow. The platform continues expanding its capabilities across prospecting, lead qualification, deal summaries, predictive scoring, and follow up generation. One particularly useful feature pulls information from previous emails, notes, and opportunity history before drafting follow up messages. That context produces emails that feel much closer to what an experienced account executive would normally write. Sales managers also benefit because opportunity summaries become much easier to review during pipeline meetings. For organizations already committed to HubSpot, the transition feels almost invisible. Best For Companies already running sales operations inside HubSpot that want built in artificial intelligence throughout the CRM experience. Key Features The biggest benefit comes from having intelligence available exactly where salespeople already work every day. Nothing feels disconnected from the rest of the sales process, making adoption much easier across larger teams. AI generated deal summaries Suggested next actions for active opportunities Breeze Prospecting Agent Personalized email drafting using CRM history Predictive lead scoring Automated enrichment of customer information Sales pipeline insights inside HubSpot AI assistance throughout contacts, deals, and company records For managers, these features reduce time spent reviewing every individual opportunity. For sales representatives, they remove much of the repetitive writing and administrative work that slowly fills every afternoon. Pricing Breeze capabilities are available across several HubSpot plans. Most advanced sales functionality becomes available through Sales Hub, beginning around $90 per user each month. Limitations The platform delivers its greatest value inside the HubSpot ecosystem. Organizations using Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, or other CRMs will not experience the same seamless workflow. Most features also remain user initiated. The assistant appears while salespeople work inside HubSpot rather than completing large amounts of background activity independently. 4. Salesforce Agentforce Salesforce has spent years developing artificial intelligence through Einstein. Agentforce expands that vision considerably. Rather than simply recommending actions, the platform introduces autonomous agents capable of completing many repetitive CRM tasks across the sales process. Large enterprise organizations often struggle with CRM maintenance. Agentforce helps reduce many of those issues through intelligent automation built directly inside Salesforce. Reps receive opportunity insights, suggested emails, conversation summaries, lead scoring, and automated record updates without leaving the CRM. Managers benefit from cleaner data while salespeople spend less time maintaining pipeline hygiene. Companies already invested heavily in Salesforce gain another advantage. No major migration project; no complicated synchronization between several systems. Everything operates inside the same environment where customer information already exists. That seamless experience makes Salesforce one of the leading Intelligent sales assistant software options for enterprise revenue organizations. Best For Enterprise sales teams already running Salesforce that want advanced automation, predictive insights, and AI assistance embedded throughout their CRM. Key Features Salesforce continues expanding its artificial intelligence portfolio beyond forecasting and reporting. Modern Agentforce capabilities support sales representatives throughout much larger portions of the customer journey. AI lead scoring Opportunity health analysis Automated follow up drafting Agentforce autonomous CRM actions Einstein Conversation Insights Pipeline recommendations Predictive forecasting Extensive administrative customization Enterprise grade workflow automation Organizations asking How to implement AI sales assistants to accelerate rep ramp and reduce training time? often begin with systems like Salesforce because new hires receive structured guidance inside the same CRM they use every day. Conversation insights, opportunity recommendations, and automated workflows reduce the amount of manual coaching managers need during onboarding. Pricing Einstein capabilities appear across multiple Salesforce editions. Agentforce follows a separate consumption based pricing model beginning around $2 per conversation, with enterprise bundles also available. Limitations Salesforce remains one of the most configurable CRM platforms available. That level of customization also means successful deployments require experienced administrators and clean customer data. Organizations without dedicated CRM resources may need additional implementation time before seeing the full value of Agentforce. 5. Cognism Finding accurate prospect data has never been easy. Finding accurate prospect data while staying compliant with European privacy regulations is even harder. That is the problem Cognism was built to solve. Many prospecting databases perform well in North America, but sales teams expanding into the United Kingdom and Europe often discover gaps in contact quality, mobile numbers, and compliance. Cognism has spent years building its reputation around verified B2B data, GDPR compliant prospecting, and high quality mobile numbers that outbound teams can confidently use. The platform has also invested heavily in artificial intelligence. Its AI Sales Companion analyzes successful customer accounts, identifies patterns across closed business, and recommends similar companies worth pursuing. Funding announcements, hiring activity, executive changes, company growth, and intent signals help sales teams prioritize accounts showing higher buying potential. Cognism also partners with Bombora for third party intent data, giving users another layer of insight before reaching out. For organizations selling internationally, this combination of verified data and AI driven sales intelligence and insights creates a much more efficient prospecting workflow. Best For Sales organizations targeting European markets that need verified contact data, GDPR compliant prospecting, and intelligent account recommendations. Key Features Prospecting platforms succeed when they reduce research time while improving data quality. Cognism performs particularly well across both areas, helping sales representatives spend less time validating information before launching outreach. Small workflow improvements like this reduce unnecessary context switching throughout the prospecting process. Pricing Custom pricing based on data requirements, geographic coverage, and team size. Limitations Cognism focuses heavily on prospecting and data quality. Organizations searching for meeting summaries, coaching, CRM automation, or post call productivity will usually combine it with another platform designed for those responsibilities. 6. New salespeople benefit from continuous support throughout live customer conversations, while experienced account executives receive reminders that help maintain consistency across larger sales organizations. Rather than producing a transcript and stopping there, tl;dv organizes conversations into useful business knowledge. Every meeting becomes searchable, shareable, and connected to your sales workflow. Managers can identify recurring objections across multiple deals. Product teams can review customer feedback without attending every meeting. Sales leaders can coach representatives using real customer conversations rather than relying on memory. That broader visibility makes the platform valuable far beyond note taking. Another area where tl;dv performs particularly well is CRM automation. When buyers ask, Which AI sales assistants integrate with your existing sales engagement platform? , tl;dv consistently appears near the top because of its extensive CRM support and thousands of integrations through Zapier and its API. Rather than serving individual sales representatives, the software provides visibility across the entire revenue organization. Managers gain a clearer understanding of account coverage. Revenue operations teams identify gaps before deals begin slipping. Executives receive forecasting insights supported by complete customer activity rather than incomplete CRM records. This makes People.ai one of the more valuable Intelligent sales assistant software solutions for organizations managing large sales teams where pipeline visibility carries just as much importance as prospecting. Although representatives also benefit from automatic activity capture, the platform delivers its biggest impact at the leadership level. Best For Enterprise sales organizations, revenue operations teams, and sales leaders looking for comprehensive activity capture, forecasting support, and pipeline visibility. Key Features People.ai focuses on connecting customer activity to business outcomes. Every interaction contributes to a more complete understanding of deal health across the organization. Automatic capture of emails, meetings, and phone activity Account and opportunity mapping Revenue intelligence dashboards Deal health analysis Account coverage insights Pipeline visibility Forecasting support CRM synchronization Activity analytics for sales leadership For organizations with hundreds of opportunities moving simultaneously, these insights help managers identify deals requiring attention before problems become obvious in quarterly forecasting meetings. Pricing Custom enterprise pricing. Limitations People.ai concentrates on reporting, forecasting, and revenue intelligence. Sales representatives looking for prospect databases, outbound sequencing, or live conversation coaching will usually pair it with other AI powered sales copilots designed for day to day selling activities. Choosing the Right AI Sales Assistant No single platform will suit every sales organization. Some teams spend most of their day prospecting, whereas others spend hours following up after customer meetings. That is why the first question should never be, "Which product has the most AI features?" A much better question is, "Where does our team lose the most time every week?" If prospect research consumes hours every day, Apollo.io or Cognism deserve serious consideration. If outbound calling sits at the center of your sales process, a platform like Trellus provides a much broader workspace that combines prospect research, coaching, workflow automation, and productivity inside one environment. If your entire revenue organization already operates inside HubSpot or Salesforce, their native artificial intelligence capabilities remove friction because sales representatives continue working inside familiar systems. Companies running dozens of customer meetings every week may see faster returns from tools like tl;dv or Otter.ai, while enterprise revenue teams needing complete pipeline visibility will appreciate what People.ai brings to forecasting and account management.

title: Enphase Energy Brings Its Full Home Energy Platform to Italy with Backup, Three-Phase Support, and EV Charging
summary: FREMONT, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enphase Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: ENPH), a global energy technology company, today announced that Italian homeowners can now build a complete home energy system with Enphase, combining solar, storage, backup, and EV charging on a single platform.
body_text: FREMONT, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enphase Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: ENPH), a global energy technology company, today announced that Italian homeowners can now build a complete home energy system with Enphase, combining solar, storage, backup, and EV charging on a single platform. The new IQ® System Controller 3 enables homeowners with IQ® Battery 5P™ systems to add home backup for the first time, including three-phase backup, while the IQ® EV Charger 2 lets them power their vehicle from their own solar energy. Together, the products give homeowners a future-ready system they can expand as their energy needs grow. The launch comes as Italy's electricity grid faces growing strain from extreme heat. National grid operator Terna recorded a 2026 demand peak of 55 GW on June 23, 2026, up 4.4 percent from the previous week, as a prolonged heatwave triggered power cuts in cities including Turin, Milan, Naples, and Rome. E-Distribuzione, which manages grid distribution across roughly 7,500 Italian municipalities, has acknowledged the resulting network strain and committed €2.8 billion to adapt its infrastructure to increasingly severe heatwave conditions. For homeowners already generating and storing their own solar energy, backup power means keeping essential circuits running even when the grid itself is under pressure. The IQ System Controller 3 protects a homeowner's original investment in Enphase batteries, while letting the energy system evolve as household needs grow. Customers can keep essential circuits powered during outages and add storage over time as they adopt electric vehicles, heat pumps, and other electric appliances. Italian homeowners have two flexible upgrade paths, both configured by an Enphase-certified installer through the Enphase® Installer App: Add backup. Homeowners with an IQ Battery 5P system can add the IQ System Controller 3 to keep essential loads powered during grid outages. With FlexPhase , three-phase homes can back up across all three phases, with the homeowner and installer determining which circuits remain powered. Expand storage. Homeowners can add IQ Battery 5P units to grow their storage capacity, whether the system stays grid-tied or is upgraded with backup. Existing batteries continue operating as part of the expanded system. During a grid outage, the IQ System Controller 3 disconnects the home from the grid and, using Enphase's grid-forming technology, allows the solar and battery system to continue powering the home. In Italy, the IQ System Controller 3 operates together with an external grid-protection relay to meet the interconnection requirements of the CEI 0-21 standard. The system supports both single-phase and three-phase backup, including seamless backup of three-phase loads, and can back up loads of up to 80 A per phase. The capability is available now through Enphase-certified installers using the Enphase Installer App. Homeowners interested in adding backup to a new or existing IQ Battery 5P system can contact an Enphase-certified installer. Installers can find training and system-configuration guidance at Enphase University. "We built this business by trusting Enphase to deliver on what they promise," said Fabrizio Falco, sales manager at IS Energy, an installer of Enphase products in Turin, Italy. "The IQ System Controller 3 gives us one more reason to keep that trust: real backup power we can now bring to our customers." "We're excited to bring the IQ System Controller 3 to market alongside the IQ Battery 5P," said Lorenzo Censi, sales manager at BeNext, an installer of Enphase products in Rome, Italy. "Between FlexPhase and now backup, our installers have a complete storage solution to offer, and we're ready to support them from day one." Completing the platform, homeowners in Italy can also charge their vehicle with the Enphase IQ EV Charger 2 , available across Europe since July 2026 and designed for direct sunlight and extreme climates. It can be installed as a standalone charger or paired with an Enphase solar and battery system, where green charging maximizes the share of each charge drawn from the homeowner's own solar rather than the grid, adjusting automatically as production changes and beginning from as little as approximately 1.4 kW of surplus solar. Homeowners with an Enphase battery need no additional hardware, and those with third-party solar can enable the same green charging by adding a third-party consumption meter. The charger's availability comes as Italy prepares to introduce the Bonus Colonnine 2026 incentive, a government grant expected to cover up to 80 percent of the cost of purchasing and installing a home EV charger, with final caps and eligibility to be confirmed in the implementing decrees. Homeowners interested in the IQ EV Charger 2 can contact an Enphase-certified installer for more information. "Italian homeowners can now bring together solar, storage, backup, and EV charging in one Enphase system, all from a single app," said Sabbas Daniel, senior vice president of sales at Enphase Energy. "The IQ System Controller 3 keeps the lights on when the grid goes down, including across all three phases, and the IQ EV Charger 2 lets families drive on their own sunshine. This is what a complete, future-ready home energy platform looks like." For more information about Enphase in Italy, please visit the website . About Enphase Energy, Inc. Enphase Energy, a global energy technology company based in Fremont, CA, is the world's leading supplier of microinverter-based solar and battery systems, EV chargers, home energy management systems, and virtual power plant (VPP) solutions. Enphase products enable people to harness the sun to make, use, save, and sell their own power, all controlled through the Enphase App. The company revolutionized the solar industry with its microinverter-based technology and has shipped approximately 89.4 million microinverters, with approximately 5.3 million Enphase-based systems deployed in over 165 countries. title: Mosaic and Partners Pioneer New Approach to Florida Scrub-Jay Recovery
body_text: Found nowhere else on Earth and known for its bright blue-and-white features, the Florida Scrub-Jay is the state's only endemic bird species. After losing an estimated 90 percent of its population due to loss or degradation of scrub habitat, the species is at risk. Only seven regions across Florida have enough interconnected scrub habitat to allow populations to be large enough to survive long term. However, thanks to a collaborative effort between The Mosaic Company and conservation partners, the future of the Florida Scrub-Jay in one region is showing signs of improvement. For more than 25 years, researchers, biologists and wildlife experts from Mosaic and partner organizations have worked to better understand the Florida Scrub-Jay and identify ways to grow a population in Manatee County, known as M4. “At Mosaic, environmental stewardship means taking a long-term view of the landscapes we manage and the species that depend on them,” said Dr. Boughton. “The early success of this translocation reflects more than 25 years of studying and monitoring efforts to grow the regional Florida Scrub-Jay population. Insights from translocations conducted between 2003 and 2010 helped us refine our approach, while genetic diversity studies showed there was even more we could do to support the species’ recovery.” Connecting Populations In January, researchers successfully relocated 48 Florida Scrub-Jays from three regions of the state to strengthen genetic diversity and improve the long-term health of the M4 population. Researchers selected 48 young birds entering their first breeding season to study and give the best opportunity to establish territories, choose mates and integrate together. The team translocated 16 birds from Duette Preserve in Manatee County, 16 birds from a population near Cape Canaveral on Florida's east coast, and 16 birds from Archbold Biological Station south of Lake Placid to Wingate Creek State Park in Manatee County in January 2026. All 48 birds survived the initial move and are being closely monitored. Researchers have already observed nesting activity during the birds' first breeding season in their new locations at higher levels than expected. This project marked the largest single translocation of Florida Scrub-Jays to ever occur. “We want to follow them over the next two to three years and see if we can retain those same pairs on site having future generations producing offspring and that's the success there,” said Todd Mecklenborg, Wildlife Biologist, U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service. “This might be a new innovative approach on how we approach areas where the numbers are way down or we want to build up a more resilient population.” The Florida Scrub-Jay depends on the state's rare scrub habitat and there are only seven regions across Florida that contain enough interconnected scrub habitat to support large enough populations for long-term population survival. Habitat Reclamation Was Key The Florida Scrub-Jay lives in the state's rare scrub habitat. Mosaic has spent more than 25 years leading efforts to protect one regional population of the Florida Scrub-Jay by working with government agencies, scientists and conservation partners. Mosaic helped build a regional approach that restores critical scrub habitat, an ecosystem increasingly impacted by development and fire suppression, and has significantly increased the scrub-jay population through those efforts. “This study not only highlights the progress we've made but also informs future strategies to further enhance the genetic health of translocated populations,” said Dr. Boughton. “It's an example of how responsible land management can go hand-in-hand with conservation, benefiting biodiversity while allowing for sustainable development.” Mosaic-supported research shows that Florida Scrub-Jay population growth alone isn't enough. Genetic diversity is critical to long-term survival. This translocation effort is expected to improve the population's genetic diversity in the M4 population, a key factor in long-term survival. “Small populations are really vulnerable to lots of different environmental effects,” said Lauren Deaner, Ph.D. Candidate, University of Central Florida. “You're constantly fighting those environmental factors in order to try to bring up population numbers but also increase the genetic diversity, and that's what we are doing here.” (Left to right) Raoul Boughton, Ph.D., Senior Manager – Ecology & Wildlife, Mosaic; Sahas Barve, Ph.D., Archbold Biological Station; Lauren Deaner, Senior Ecologist – Verdantas and Ph.D. Candidate, Biology – UCF; Todd Mecklenborg, Wildlife Biologist, U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service. Working Together The project represents a significant collaboration among public and private partners, including The Mosaic Company, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Verdantas, the University of Central Florida and Archbold Biological Station. Regional contributions from Manatee County, Southwest Florida Water Management District, Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and regional land managers were also instrumental in preparing and maintaining suitable habitat conditions. title: 9 things to look for when choosing new POS for your restaurant
summary: Searching for a POS for your restaurant? These 9 considerations should be taken into account when making the all-important investment in the right point of sale.
body_text: You have enough on your plate, get a POS that runs the store end-to-end! As a restaurant owner or operator, you’re looking for opportunities to improve the customer experience and differentiate your dining experience. You likely want to give customers choice, speed and accuracy while freeing up staff so they can spend more time with guests. Having a restaurant POS system that helps you offer that will set you up to better run your restaurant—so you can focus on what matters most. If you’re a restaurant owner or operator we don’t have to tell you: running a restaurant is not an easy task! But having technology that’ll help your operations run smoother and enables your staff to be efficient so they can focus on delivering a memorable experience can help. When researching a new restaurant point-of-sale system, it’s important to keep key features in mind to ensure your operation is set up for success. Here are nine things to look for when choosing a new POS for your restaurant. Technology that… 1. Enables you to add additional revenue streams into your restaurant beyond in-store. Gone are the days where the restaurant experience is primarily in-store dining. Now consumers are looking for digital ordering and delivery too. The flexibility to add services such as takeout, mobile ordering, loyalty and 3rd party partners is important to ensure your restaurant is supported to expand your business. This can help you increase same-store sales right out of the box. 2. Supports mobile POS for tableside ordering or line busting. You want tech that eliminates the steps between the table and kitchen, helping speed up service so you can take several more orders each day. 3. Makes training and implementation easy for you and your staff. Having a system that’s easy-to-learn and adopt can help improve staff and management productivity levels. You want tech that your staff can easily manage, but that can also maintain even the most complex operations. 4. Supports conversational ordering. This ensures your servers and cashiers capture all aspects of the order, including sides, modifiers, etc., maintaining accuracy. For takeout and catering, you want the ability to capture future orders and keep track of customer information including order history. 5. Provides payment flexibility and security to help reduce liability from potential chargebacks. You want to be able to securely accept the variety of payment types that your customer wants to use, including mobile wallets and pay-at-table. 6. Has a cloud-based centralized system configuration and management. This allows operators to push out menu changes such as new items, discontinuations and price changes, automatically from a central location. This provides operators flexibility to make changes anywhere, anytime. 7. Keeps your technology up-to-date with the ever-evolving market. You want your tech to stay current with continuous updates of the latest versions and patches for both software and hardware. 8. Has redundancy and durability in the event of a failover. Things can happen, whether it’s losing your internet connection or your devices fail. You want technology that has terminal failover redundancy so that you never lose a transaction. 9. Gives access to real-time data so you have a constant pulse on your business. Having immediate visibility into how your restaurant is performing is important as an operator. You’ll want technology that delivers you real-time alerts and instant access to sales data from your mobile device. You have enough on your plate, get a POS that runs the store end-to-end! As a restaurant owner or operator, you’re looking for opportunities to improve the customer experience and differentiate your dining experience. You likely want to give customers choice, speed and accuracy while freeing up staff so they can spend more time with guests. Having a restaurant POS system that helps you offer that will set you up to better run your restaurant—so you can focus on what matters most.

summary: Mythic Action Epic Delivers $37 Million Worldwide in IMAX in its Fourth Frame, Lifting IMAX to its Fourth Consecutive $50 Million -Plus Weekend NEW YORK --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 10, 2026-- The record-breaking run of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in IMAX (NYSE: IMAX) reached yet another new
body_text: Mythic Action Epic Delivers $37 Million Worldwide in IMAX in its Fourth Frame, Lifting IMAX to its Fourth Consecutive $50 Million-Plus Weekend NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 10, 2026-- The record-breaking run of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in IMAX (NYSE: IMAX) reached yet another new milestone this weekend, taking the crown as the highest grossing IMAX release of all time with $289 million in less than a month of play. The mythic action epic earned another $37 million worldwide on IMAX screens, which account for more than 26% of the film’s overall global box office across its run to date. The strong performance lifted IMAX to an astounding fourth consecutive weekend of $50 million-plus at the global box office with $52 million worldwide; prior to the release of The Odyssey , IMAX had never delivered even two $50 million weekends in a row. “On behalf of IMAX, I want to extend our congratulations and deepest gratitude to Chris, Emma, the entire team behind The Odyssey and our friends at Universal on this monumental achievement — shattering our longstanding box office record with at least a month left to run on IMAX screens worldwide,” said Rich Gelfond, CEO of IMAX. “We had the very highest of hopes for The Odyssey from the start, but it somehow continues to exceed them, and its historic performance is headlining what we expect will be our best year ever at the global box office.” In North America, The Odyssey generated $9 million, lifting its Domestic total to $147 million in IMAX – the highest grossing Domestic release of all time. Internationally, the film earned $28.5 million including its debut in South Korea, where it achieved the highest grossing IMAX opening weekend ever in the market. IMAX 70mm Film locations, the gold-standard 18K presentation available at just 41 IMAX auditoriums worldwide, have grossed an astounding $37.5 million to date, led by the iconic TCL Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles, which has grossed $2.8 million to date – the highest grossing single-title box office for any IMAX location in North America. With nearly $40 million in pre-sales for future showtimes and sellouts for weeks in advance, The Odyssey will continue to play in the IMAX global network through at least September 17. The film is also still set to debut in China next weekend and Japan in September, continuing an unprecedented global run. The mythic action epic — for which IMAX developed a next-generation film camera and state-of-the-art technology enabling sync sound — is the first theatrical release shot entirely with IMAX Film Cameras. Christopher Nolan and cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema collaborated with IMAX to develop The Keighley, a next-generation IMAX Film Camera, along with a new sound blimp compatible with multiple IMAX Film Cameras, which together shot a total of 2.1 million feet of IMAX film in the making of The Odyssey . IMAX’s strong weekend results were further bolstered by Spider-Man: Brand New Day which debuted on IMAX screens in North America to $9.8 million and earned an additional $3.8 million in China and Japan. The film has now earned over $42 million to date in IMAX. About IMAX Corporation IMAX (NYSE: IMAX) is a global leader in entertainment technology, delivering immersive cinematic experiences through proprietary software, architecture, and projection systems. Filmmakers, studios, and artists worldwide use IMAX to connect with audiences at scale, making its network one of the most powerful platforms for blockbuster events and entertainment. Headquartered in New York, Toronto, and Los Angeles, IMAX operates 1,876 systems across 91 countries and territories as of June 30, 2026. title: 9 Best Sales Enablement Platforms for Outbound Teams: 2026 Comparison
summary: Although sales enablement tools are going by dime a dozen these days, we zeroed in one some of the best software that are known for boosting conversions, performance and business scalability. Read on...
body_text: A few years ago, most companies viewed sales enablement as a place to store training videos, onboarding documents, and a few playbooks. It was useful, but it rarely influenced revenue in a measurable way. Naturally, as things progressed over time, the typical mindset around different solutions also changed. Today's outbound organizations expect far more from their technology. Managers want to coach representatives in real time. Sales leaders want visibility into what separates top performers from everyone else. Marketing wants proof that content contributes to pipeline. Revenue leaders want platforms that shorten onboarding, improve talk track consistency, and help every representative perform closer to the level of the company's best sellers. The numbers explain why expectations have changed so dramatically. Forrester reported in late 2025 that only 23% of sales enablement deployments reached their expected ROI during the first year. The remaining 77% stalled because adoption remained low, implementation became too complicated, or the platform addressed the wrong problems. Also Read: 10 Best Digital Sales Enablement Tools to Boost Productivity Sales Enablement KPIs: Key Metrics to Measure Sales Success Those findings tell an important story. Buying more software does not automatically create a better outbound organization. Teams need technology that becomes part of everyday selling, coaching, prospecting, and performance improvement. If representatives stop opening the platform after onboarding, its value disappears quickly. The best sales enablement platforms for outbound teams have moved well beyond content libraries. They connect coaching, call intelligence, outbound execution, learning, performance analytics, and sales content into one continuous workflow. Every conversation teaches the platform something new, and every coaching session helps representatives perform better during the next call. Throughout this comparison, you'll see platforms serving different parts of the outbound motion. Some specialize in coaching. Others focus on content management. Several concentrate on conversation intelligence or learning management. Understanding those differences makes choosing the right platform much easier. What is Sales Enablement Software, Or Platform For That Matter? Sales enablement software refers to technology designed to help revenue teams sell more effectively throughout the entire customer journey. Rather than serving as a single application, most modern platforms combine several capabilities into one workspace. These typically include onboarding, continuous learning, coaching, content management, playbooks, conversation intelligence, analytics, and CRM connectivity. The purpose is straightforward. Representatives should spend less time searching for information and more time speaking with qualified prospects. Managers should spend less time manually reviewing calls and more time coaching behaviors that improve performance. Marketing teams should understand which content contributes to revenue instead of relying on assumptions. Modern Sales enablement software for outbound teams supports every stage of the sales process, from onboarding a new SDR to improving objection handling months after they join the organization. Many platforms also combine several familiar business systems into one environment. These commonly include: Learning Management Systems that deliver onboarding, certifications, product training, and continuous education. Content Management Systems that organize sales collateral, presentations, playbooks, battle cards, and case studies. CRM integrations that connect enablement activity directly to opportunities, meetings, pipeline progression, and revenue outcomes. AI coaching engines that review conversations, identify skill gaps, recommend improvements, and reinforce successful selling behaviors. Although the technology has become considerably more sophisticated, the objective remains simple. Give every seller immediate access to the knowledge, coaching, and content they need before, during, and after every conversation. Editor’s Picks: Best Sales Enablement Platforms Worth Trying In 2026 Here’s a complete rundown of the best programs that are available right now for all kinds of sales first businesses. Do keep in mind that none of the features make them a good or bad choice for your business. You need to look at your workflow, business requirements and budget, and then match these baseline aspects against whatever features different tools are offering. Once everything seems in order, feel free to move to a new program and take things forward from there. 1.
